# Data

Let's get the data first.

```{r}
sp <- read_csv(file.path(cfg$project$data,"imagery_zooscan_samples+acquisitions_cleaned.csv"))
obj <- read_csv(file.path(cfg$project$data,"imagery_zooscan_objects_morpho_taxo_cleaned.csv")) %>%
  select(sampleid,acquisid,grey_median,scientificname,class_phylum:family_order) %>% 
  left_join(select(sp,sampleid,genid,acquisid,d))
```

Let's create synthetic mean grey that are associated with each scientificname and higher taxonomic levels:

```{r}
# scientificname 
scmean <- obj %>%
  group_by(genid,scientificname) %>%
  summarize(sample_class_adjmean=sum(grey_median*d)/sum(d)) %>%
  group_by(scientificname) %>% 
  summarize(mean_scientificname=mean(sample_class_adjmean))

# family
fammean <- obj %>%
  group_by(genid,family_order) %>%
  summarize(sample_class_adjmean=sum(grey_median*d)/sum(d)) %>%
  group_by(family_order) %>% 
  summarize(mean_family=mean(sample_class_adjmean))

# order
ordermean <- obj %>%
  group_by(genid,order_class) %>%
  summarize(sample_class_adjmean=sum(grey_median*d)/sum(d)) %>%
  group_by(order_class) %>% 
  summarize(mean_order=mean(sample_class_adjmean))

# class
clmean <- obj %>%
  group_by(genid,class_phylum_detailed_copepods) %>%
  summarize(sample_class_adjmean=sum(grey_median*d)/sum(d)) %>%
  group_by(class_phylum_detailed_copepods) %>% 
  summarize(mean_class=mean(sample_class_adjmean))

# grouped class
phylmean <- obj %>%
  group_by(genid,class_phylum) %>%
  summarize(sample_class_adjmean=sum(grey_median*d)/sum(d)) %>%
  group_by(class_phylum) %>% 
  summarize(mean_phylum=mean(sample_class_adjmean))
```

# 

# Reconstructing a sample average grey

To reconstruct a sample's mean grey level, we can use: individual levels, or associate to abundances a value per scientificname, family, order, class or phylum.

This is especially important when modelling, where you cannot model an infinite number of classes.

```{r}
fake <- obj %>% 
  # add all the synthetic grey means 
  left_join(scmean) %>% 
  left_join(fammean) %>%
  left_join(ordermean) %>%
  left_join(clmean) %>%
  left_join(phylmean) %>%
  # calculate the reconstructed sample mean grey for each 
  pivot_longer(c(grey_median,mean_phylum,mean_class,mean_order,mean_family,mean_scientificname),names_to="base",values_to="value") %>% 
  group_by(genid,base) %>% 
  summarize(reconstructed=sum(value*d)/sum(d)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from="base",values_from="reconstructed") %>%
  # associate to each real sample mean grey (grey_median) the reconstructed ones
  pivot_longer(mean_class:mean_scientificname,names_to="base",values_to="reconstructed")

# plot 
fake %>% 
  mutate(base=factor(base,levels=c("mean_phylum","mean_class","mean_order","mean_family","mean_scientificname"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=grey_median,y=reconstructed,color=base)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(color="grey") + 
  #stat_regline_equation() + 
  stat_cor(aes(label = ..rr.label..), label.x = 180, label.y = 140) +  
  geom_smooth(se=FALSE,color="black",method="lm") + 
  facet_wrap(.~base) + 
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(legend.position="none")
```

This shows 2 things:

-   first, there is an important difference between real sample average grey, and reconstructed ones, even at the scientificname level, this shows important intra-class and individual level variation

-   second, using scientificname and family does not change much in terms of accuracy, and there is another drop of accuracy when using order, class or phylum

```{r}
# plot 
fake %>% 
  mutate(base=factor(base,levels=c("mean_phylum","mean_class","mean_order","mean_family","mean_scientificname"))) %>%
  filter(base %in% c("mean_scientificname","mean_class")) %>% 
  mutate(base=if_else(base=="mean_scientificname","Scientific Name","Class/Phylum")) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=grey_median,y=reconstructed)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(color="grey") + 
  #stat_regline_equation() + 
  stat_cor(aes(label = ..rr.label..), label.x = 190, label.y = 160) +  
  geom_smooth(se=FALSE,color="black",method="lm") + 
  facet_wrap(.~base,ncol=2) + 
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(legend.position="none",
        text=element_text(size=15)) + 
    labs(x="Organism-based sample average gray",
         y="Taxonomic-based sample average grey")
```

```{r}
ggsave(file.path(cfg$project$figures,"FigSXa_reconstructed_averages.tiff"),dpi=300,width=7,height=4)
```

We can have a look at it by biomes and oceans:

```{r}
sps <- read_csv(file.path(cfg$project$data,"imagery_zooscan_samples_marine_regions+daytime.csv"))

fake %>% 
  left_join(sps) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=grey_median,y=reconstructed,color=base)) +
  geom_abline() + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(se=FALSE,color="grey") + 
  facet_grid(base~biome) + 
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(legend.position="none")

fake %>% 
  left_join(sps) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=grey_median,y=reconstructed,color=base)) +
  geom_abline() + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(se=FALSE,color="grey") + 
  facet_grid(base~ocean_seas) + 
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(legend.position="none")
```
